title: Ecosystem Balance
description: Manage a delicate ecosystem by placing plants and animals strategically. Balance predators, prey, and vegetation to create a thriving habitat.
learning_objectives: Understand how ecosystem balance depends on the relationship between predators, prey, and vegetation
Learn how food chains connect organisms and sustain biodiversity in a habitat
Explore the importance of biodiversity and why diverse species make ecosystems more resilient
Practice habitat management by deciding where to place species for maximum ecological benefit
Recognize how removing or adding one species can cause cascading effects throughout an ecosystem
Develop strategic thinking about resource competition and territorial dynamics in nature
how_to_play: You and the AI take turns placing markers on a 9x9 habitat grid. You place species (plants and animals) to build a thriving ecosystem; the AI introduces predator threats that destabilize it.
Surround empty intersections with your species to claim that territory as Thriving Habitat — a balanced zone where life flourishes!
If you completely surround a cluster of Predator Threat markers (no empty adjacent spaces), those predators are driven out — the ecosystem reclaims its balance!
The Ko rule prevents you from immediately replanting a zone that was just disrupted, simulating the recovery time ecosystems need after a disturbance.
The game ends when both sides pass consecutively, meaning the habitat map is settled.

Thriving Habitat territory earns 1 point, and each captured predator threat earns 2 points. The predators get a 6.5 point komi head start. Build a more balanced ecosystem than they can disrupt to win!

storybook_pages.title: A World in Balance
storybook_pages.text: A vast wilderness stretches across the grid — rivers, meadows, and forests teeming with life. But the balance is fragile. Apex predators are moving in, threatening to overwhelm the delicate food web. As the Ecosystem Manager, you must place plants and animals in the right spots to keep the habitat thriving. Every species you place strengthens the web of life.
storybook_pages.image_prompt: vibrant ecosystem viewed from above forming a 9x9 grid with rivers meadows and forests, diverse animals and plants visible, a wolf silhouette approaching from the edge, a child in a green ranger outfit standing ready, bright educational cartoon style for kids

storybook_pages.title: The Food Chain Connection
storybook_pages.text: Every living thing is connected. Plants feed the herbivores, herbivores feed the predators, and when predators are kept in check, the whole system thrives. When you place species next to each other, you build food chains that support the entire habitat. But if predators break through your network, the chain collapses. Think about how each species connects to the others!
storybook_pages.image_prompt: colorful illustrated food chain diagram overlaid on a grid with plants at the bottom connecting to rabbits and deer then to wolves, some chains broken with worried animals, arrows showing energy flow, educational kids cartoon style

storybook_pages.title: Biodiversity Wins
storybook_pages.text: As the grid fills up, every placement matters more. A single well-placed species can connect two habitats and save an entire region. Sometimes you need to sacrifice a small patch to protect the heart of the ecosystem. Think like a real ecologist — prioritize biodiversity and balance. The strongest ecosystems are the most diverse ones.

glossary_terms.definition: The process of selecting among alternatives based on available information and values.
glossary_terms.example: Choosing between two career paths based on income, passion, and long-term growth.
glossary_terms.deep_dive: Good decision-making combines rational analysis with awareness of cognitive biases that distort judgment.
glossary_terms.real_world_example: Leaders make high-stakes decisions daily — the quality of their process matters as much as the decision itself.

glossary_terms.definition: Analyzing information objectively to form a well-reasoned judgment.
glossary_terms.example: Questioning whether a statistic is representative before using it to make a decision.
glossary_terms.deep_dive: Critical thinking involves identifying assumptions, evaluating evidence, and considering alternative perspectives.
glossary_terms.real_world_example: Journalists fact-check before publishing; scientists replicate experiments before claiming discoveries.

glossary_terms.definition: The belief that abilities can be developed through effort and learning from failure.
glossary_terms.example: Seeing a poor game result as feedback on what to practice, not evidence of being bad at the game.
glossary_terms.deep_dive: Research by Carol Dweck shows people with growth mindsets achieve more and recover better from setbacks.
glossary_terms.real_world_example: Students who believe intelligence is fixed give up when challenged; those with growth mindset persist and improve.
